records.literal_gloss: A psalm of David, when he fled from before Absalom his son.

en.L: A psalm of David, when he fled from before Absalom his son.
en.B: A psalm of David, when he fled from his son Absalom.
en.R: A song of David, from the time he ran away from his son Absalom.

fr.L: Un psaume de David, quand il s’enfuit de devant Absalom, son fils.
fr.B: Un psaume de David, lorsqu’il s’enfuit loin de son fils Absalom.
fr.R: Un chant de David, du temps où il a fui loin de son fils Absalom.

sw.L: Zaburi ya Daudi, alipokimbia kutoka mbele ya Absalomu mwanawe.
sw.B: Zaburi ya Daudi, alipomkimbia mwanawe Absalomu.
sw.R: Wimbo wa Daudi, kutoka wakati alipomkimbia mwanawe Absalomu.

es.L: Salmo de David, cuando huyó de delante de Absalón su hijo.
es.B: Salmo de David, cuando huyó de su hijo Absalón.
es.R: Canto de David, de cuando escapó de su hijo Absalón.

vi.L: [Một] thi thiên của Đa-vít, khi ông chạy trốn khỏi trước mặt Áp-sa-lôm, con trai ông.
vi.B: Thi thiên của Đa-vít, khi ông chạy trốn Áp-sa-lôm, con trai mình.
vi.R: Bài ca của Đa-vít, vào lúc ông phải bỏ chạy khỏi Áp-sa-lôm, con trai mình.

ko.L: 다윗의 시, 그가 그의 아들 압살롬 앞에서 도망할 때.
ko.B: 다윗의 시. 그가 아들 압살롬을 피해 도망할 때.
ko.R: 다윗이 지은 노래. 아들 압살롬을 피해 도망치던 때의 노래.

pt.L: Salmo de Davi, quando ele fugiu de diante de Absalão, seu filho.
pt.B: Salmo de Davi, quando fugiu do seu filho Absalão.
pt.R: Canção de Davi, do tempo em que ele fugiu do seu filho Absalão.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text the title of a psalm is part of the psalm and is counted as its first verse, so from Psalm 3 on the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number (Psalm 3:2 here is 3:1 there). Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates.

decisions.choice: psalm: a song sung to music
decisions.reason: The word (mizmor) is used only in psalm titles, for a song sung with instruments. The book's Greek name, Psalms, comes from the Greek word for such songs.

decisions.choice: of David: belonging to David
decisions.reason: The small word "of" (le-) can mean written by, belonging to, for or about. The title ties the psalm to David and to a time in his life.

decisions.choice: when he fled from Absalom: 2 Samuel 15-17
decisions.reason: David's son Absalom turned the people against his father and was made king in Hebron. David fled from Jerusalem across the Jordan, with crowds against him (2 Samuel 15:12-14; 17:11). The psalm's many enemies (verses 2, 7) fit that time.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: Readable says what a psalm is (m2).

decisions.choice: titles: "Un psaume" (Literal, Balanced), "Un chant" (Readable); the event a title recalls in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced, the passé composé at Readable; the psalms themselves in the tenses of speech (present, passé composé, future) at every level
alternatives: the passé simple inside the psalms
decisions.reason: A title points to a story told elsewhere (2 Samuel 15-17), so it follows the French tenses of narrative by level. The psalms are prayer and song, spoken to God or about him, so they keep the tenses of speech, as the song of Exodus 15 does.

decisions.choice: "Zaburi" for mizmor at Literal and Balanced; "wimbo" (song) at Readable, in every title
decisions.reason: "Zaburi" is the Swahili name for a psalm and for the book itself; Readable says "wimbo", the everyday word for a song sung to music, as the English Readable says "song".

decisions.choice: Salmo (L, B); Canto (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew mizmor is a song sung to music. Literal and Balanced say "Salmo", Readable "Canto", as the English says "psalm" and "song". In a title Spanish leaves out the article, so "Salmo de David" rather than "Un salmo de David".

decisions.choice: "thi thiên" (L, B), "bài ca" (R), as Psalm 23:1; "Áp-sa-lôm" for Absalom
decisions.reason: The titles of this block follow the published Psalms: "thi thiên" is the word Bible readers know, and Readable says "bài ca" (song) as the English Readable says "song". Absalom takes the Protestant tradition's form of the name.

decisions.choice: Titles: "다윗의 시" (L, B), "다윗이 지은 노래" (R); Absalom is "압살롬"
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 7a) and the published Psalm 23: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's "psalm of David", Readable calls it a song David made, as the English Readable says "song". The title is verse 1 and stays prose. This holds for the titles of Psalms 3-25.

decisions.choice: Salmo de Davi (L, B); Canção de Davi (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the title formula is "Salmo de Davi", without an article, as Portuguese writes titles (the English "A psalm" has none in brackets either). Readable says "Canção", as the English Readable says "song" (m2); "cântico" is kept for the Hebrew shir ("Cântico dos degraus").

source.text: יְ֭הוָה מָֽה־רַבּ֣וּ צָרָ֑י רַ֝בִּ֗ים קָמִ֥ים עָלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH, how many are my foes! Many [are] rising against me.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, how many my foes have become! \q Many [are] rising up against me.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, how my enemies have multiplied! \q Many are rising up against me.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I have so many enemies! \q So many people are turning against me.

fr.L: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, combien mes adversaires sont devenus nombreux ! \q Nombreux [sont ceux qui] se lèvent contre moi.
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, comme mes ennemis se sont multipliés ! \q Ils sont nombreux à se dresser contre moi.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai tellement d’ennemis ! \q Tant de gens se tournent contre moi.

sw.L: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, jinsi walivyoongezeka watesi wangu! \q Wengi wanainuka dhidi yangu.
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, adui zangu wameongezeka kama nini! \q Wengi wanainuka kunipinga.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nina adui wengi mno! \q Watu wengi sana wananigeukia.

es.L: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡qué numerosos se han vuelto mis adversarios! \q Muchos [están] levantándose contra mí.
es.B: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡cuánto han aumentado mis enemigos! \q Muchos se alzan contra mí.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡tengo tantos enemigos! \q Muchísima gente se está poniendo en mi contra.

vi.L: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, kẻ thù của tôi đã trở nên nhiều biết bao! \q Nhiều kẻ [đang] nổi lên chống lại tôi.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, kẻ thù của tôi sao đông đến thế! \q Biết bao kẻ đang nổi dậy chống lại tôi.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, tôi có quá nhiều kẻ thù! \q Biết bao người đang quay lại chống tôi.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제 대적들이 어찌 그리 많아졌습니까! \q 많은 사람이 저를 거슬러 일어납니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제 원수들이 어찌 이리도 많아졌습니까! \q 많은 사람이 저를 거슬러 일어섭니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제게 원수가 너무나 많습니다! \q 너무나 많은 사람이 저에게 등을 돌립니다.

pt.L: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, quão numerosos se tornaram os meus adversários! \q Muitos [estão] se levantando contra mim.
pt.B: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, como aumentaram os meus inimigos! \q Muitos estão se levantando contra mim.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, eu tenho tantos inimigos! \q Tanta gente está se voltando contra mim.

decisions.choice: rising up against me: rebelling against me
decisions.reason: To rise up against someone (qum 'al) is to attack or rebel. It is the phrase used of Absalom's rebels in 2 Samuel 18:31-32: "all who rose up against you".

decisions.choice: how many: a cry of dismay
decisions.reason: The line is an exclamation. The word "many" is repeated three times in verses 2-3 (many my foes, many rising, many saying), piling up the numbers against one man.

decisions.choice: LORD, (in address)
decisions.reason: When the psalmist speaks to God by name, the name stands alone, without "O" or "the"; the divine name setting still offers Yahweh.

decisions.choice: in address, "SEIGNEUR" without the article ("Yahvé" as the alternative), and "tu" to God throughout the Psalms
decisions.reason: French calls on someone without an article, as the English drops "the". The psalmist speaks to God with "tu", the ordinary French of prayer in this translation, as people speak to Jesus in the Gospels.

decisions.choice: "Ee BWANA" in address at Literal and Balanced; "BWANA," alone at Readable
decisions.reason: "Ee" is the Swahili word that marks a call to someone, used in prayer; Readable leaves it out, as everyday speech does.

decisions.choice: "Lạy CHÚA" when the psalmist calls on God by name, unbracketed at Literal
decisions.reason: Vietnamese calls on God with "Lạy", a word of address the grammar of prayer requires, as in the published Psalm 139:1; the psalmist then speaks to God as "Ngài", with the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: Speaking to God the psalmist uses 합쇼체 and calls himself "저/제"; God is called "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여" and addressed as "주님"
decisions.reason: Terms note and style guide section 7a, as the published Psalms 23 and 139. Korean addresses a superior by title, not by a pronoun; the vocative "여" stands outside the span and fits both forms. Where a psalm speaks about God rather than to him, the plain written style with "나" returns (verse 5). This holds for Psalms 3-25.

decisions.choice: SENHOR, (in address), with "Javé" as the alternative
decisions.reason: For the whole book: when the psalmist speaks to God by name, the name stands alone, without "ó" or an article, as in the English (r-en-1) and in David's prayer in 1 Chronicles 17; the span still offers "Javé".

source.text: רַבִּים֮ אֹמְרִ֪ים לְנַ֫פְשִׁ֥י אֵ֤ין יְֽשׁוּעָ֓תָה לּ֬וֹ בֵֽאלֹהִ֬ים סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Many [are] saying of my soul, there is no salvation for him in God. Selah.

en.L: Many [are] saying of my soul, \q "There is no salvation for him in God." Selah
en.B: Many are saying about me, \q "God is not going to rescue him." Selah
en.R: Many people say that God will not save me. Selah

fr.L: Nombreux [sont ceux qui] disent de mon âme : \q « Il n’y a pas de salut pour lui en Dieu. » Sélah
fr.B: Beaucoup disent à mon sujet : \q « Dieu ne va pas le délivrer. » Sélah
fr.R: Beaucoup de gens disent que Dieu ne me sauvera pas. Sélah

sw.L: Wengi wanasema juu ya nafsi yangu, \q "Hakuna wokovu kwake katika Mungu." Sela
sw.B: Wengi wanasema juu yangu, \q "Mungu hatamwokoa." Sela
sw.R: Watu wengi wanasema kwamba Mungu hataniokoa. Sela

es.L: Muchos [están] diciendo de mi alma: \q «No hay salvación para él en Dios». Selah
es.B: Muchos dicen de mí: \q «Dios no lo va a rescatar». Selah
es.R: Mucha gente dice que Dios no me va a salvar. Selah

vi.L: Nhiều kẻ [đang] nói về linh hồn tôi: \q "Chẳng có sự cứu rỗi nào cho hắn nơi Đức Chúa Trời." Sê-la
vi.B: Nhiều kẻ nói về tôi: \q "Đức Chúa Trời sẽ chẳng giải cứu hắn đâu." Sê-la
vi.R: Nhiều người nói rằng Đức Chúa Trời sẽ không cứu tôi. Sê-la

ko.L: 많은 사람이 제 영혼에 대해 말합니다. \q "그에게는 하나님 안에 구원이 없다." 셀라
ko.B: 많은 사람이 저를 두고 말합니다. \q "하나님께서 그를 구해 주지 않으실 것이다." 셀라
ko.R: 많은 사람이 하나님께서 저를 구원하지 않으실 거라고 말합니다. 셀라

pt.L: Muitos [estão] dizendo da minha alma: \q "Não há salvação para ele em Deus." Selá
pt.B: Muitos dizem a meu respeito: \q "Deus não vai livrá-lo." Selá
pt.R: Muita gente diz que Deus não vai me salvar. Selá

decisions.choice: of my soul: about me
decisions.reason: The soul (nefesh) is the whole living person, so "my soul" often means "me". The words "to my soul" may mean "about me" or "to me"; the enemies speak of him as "him", so they speak about him.

decisions.choice: salvation: rescue from danger
decisions.reason: The word (yeshu'ah) is rescue from danger or defeat; here, rescue from his enemies. The psalm ends with the same word: salvation belongs to the LORD (verse 9). The enemies say that God has abandoned David, perhaps because of his sins (2 Samuel 16:7-8).

decisions.choice: God is not going to rescue him (B); God will not save me (R)
alternatives: There is no salvation for him in God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the noun into a verb with God as its subject; Literal keeps "salvation", the word that returns in verse 9.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: "Sélah" kept at the end of the verse at every level, for this block of psalms
decisions.reason: The meaning of the word is no longer known; it is probably a musical direction (m3). French keeps it as a name, in its usual French spelling, where the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: "mon âme" at Literal; "à mon sujet", "me" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Nefesh is "âme" at Literal throughout these books, so the reader can follow the word; here it means "me" (m1), and the other levels say so.

decisions.choice: "Sela" kept as it is at the end of the verse, at every level
decisions.reason: Sela is the usual Swahili spelling of the Hebrew selah, a word whose meaning is no longer known; it is probably a direction for the music or the singers. Like the English, every level keeps it where it stands rather than guess at a translation.

decisions.choice: Selah
decisions.reason: Selah is a Hebrew word whose meaning is no longer known; it is probably a direction for the music or the singers. Spanish keeps it as it is, at the end of the verse, as the English does.

decisions.choice: mi alma
decisions.reason: The Hebrew nefesh is "soul", the living self. Literal keeps "alma"; Balanced and Readable say "de mí", "me", as the English says "about me".

decisions.choice: "Sê-la" kept at the end of the verse, as a word
decisions.reason: No one now knows what Selah means; it is probably a direction for the music (see the meaning decision). Vietnamese keeps the word, in the form Bible readers know, where the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: "hắn" for the psalmist in his enemies' mouth
decisions.reason: The enemies speak of him with scorn; "hắn" carries that tone, where "ông ta" would be polite.

decisions.choice: "셀라" kept as a word at the end of the verse, at every level
alternatives: a translation such as 쉼 or 반주
decisions.reason: The meaning of the Hebrew word is no longer known (meaning decision m3); it is probably a musical or liturgical direction. Korean keeps it as a sound, as the English keeps "Selah", and does not guess a meaning. This holds for every Selah in Psalms 3-25.

decisions.choice: Selá, kept at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the word's meaning is unknown (m3), so every level keeps it, as the English does, in its usual Brazilian spelling, set apart at the end of the line.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה מָגֵ֣ן בַּעֲדִ֑י כְּ֝בוֹדִ֗י וּמֵרִ֥ים רֹאשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: But you, YHWH, [are] a shield around me, my glory, and [the one] lifting up my head.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, [are] a shield about me, \q my glory, and [the one] lifting up my head.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, are a shield on every side of me. \q You are my glory, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} lift my head up again.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, protect me like a shield all around me. \q You give me honor, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} help me hold my head up again.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, [{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es] un bouclier autour de moi, \q ma gloire, et [celui qui] relève ma tête.
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es un bouclier qui m’entoure de toutes parts. \q Tu es ma gloire, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me fais relever la tête.
fr.R: Mais {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me protèges comme un bouclier tout autour de moi. \q Tu me rends l’honneur, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’aides à relever la tête.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, [u] ngao inayonizunguka, \q utukufu wangu, na [ndiwe] unayekiinua kichwa changu.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ni ngao kila upande wangu. \q Wewe ni utukufu wangu, na unakiinua kichwa changu tena.
sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, unanilinda kama ngao inayonizunguka pande zote. \q Unanipa heshima, na unanisaidia kuinua kichwa changu tena.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, [eres] escudo a mi alrededor, \q mi gloria, y el que levanta mi cabeza.
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, eres un escudo que me rodea por todos lados. \q Tú eres mi gloria, y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} vuelves a levantar mi cabeza.
es.R: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, me proteges como un escudo a mi alrededor. \q Tú me das honra, y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me ayudas a levantar la cabeza otra vez.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, [là] cái khiên bao quanh tôi, \q [là] vinh quang của tôi, và [là Đấng] ngẩng đầu tôi lên.
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, là cái khiên che chở tôi mọi phía. \q Ngài là vinh quang của tôi, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm cho tôi ngẩng đầu lên lại.
vi.R: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, bảo vệ tôi như cái khiên bao bọc quanh tôi. \q Ngài ban cho tôi danh dự, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giúp tôi ngẩng đầu lên lại.

ko.L: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님은 제 주위를 두르는 방패, \q 저의 영광, 제 머리를 드시는 분이십니다.
ko.B: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서는 사방에서 저를 지키는 방패이십니다. \q 주님은 저의 영광이시며, 제 머리를 다시 들게 하시는 분이십니다.
ko.R: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서는 방패처럼 사방에서 저를 지켜 주십니다. \q 주님께서 저를 존귀하게 하시고, 제가 다시 고개를 들 수 있게 도와주십니다.

pt.L: Mas {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, [és] um escudo ao meu redor, \q a minha glória, e [aquele que] levanta a minha cabeça.
pt.B: Mas {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, és um escudo que me protege de todos os lados. \q Tu és a minha glória, e {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me fazes erguer de novo a cabeça.
pt.R: Mas {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, me proteges como um escudo à minha volta. \q Tu me dás honra, e {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me ajudas a erguer a cabeça de novo.

decisions.choice: a shield around me: protection on every side
decisions.reason: The shield (magen) was a small round shield carried into battle. The LORD is a shield not only in front but "around" him (Genesis 15:1, "I am your shield").

decisions.choice: my glory: the one who gives me honor
decisions.reason: Glory (kavod) is weight, honor, standing. David had lost his throne and his honor; the LORD is his honor still, and the one who will restore it. It may also mean the one in whom he takes pride.

decisions.choice: lifts up my head: restores honor and hope
decisions.reason: A bowed or covered head is a sign of shame or grief: David climbed the Mount of Olives with his head covered (2 Samuel 15:30). To lift someone's head is to restore him (Genesis 40:13).

decisions.choice: lift my head up again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "again", since the head is raised after shame (m3).

decisions.choice: You give me honor
decisions.reason: Readable says what "my glory" means here (m2).

decisions.choice: tú
decisions.reason: The psalmist speaks to God with "tú", the ordinary second person of prayer in Spanish, close and direct, as the Hebrew is. "Usted" would sound distant in prayer. The pronoun takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "cái khiên" for the shield
decisions.reason: "khiên" is the everyday word for a shield; "thuẫn" is the older literary word many readers know from church but would not use themselves. The terms note keeps "cái khiên" for the whole book.

source.text: ק֭וֹלִי אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֶקְרָ֑א וַיַּֽעֲנֵ֨נִי מֵהַ֖ר קָדְשׁ֣וֹ סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: [With] my voice to YHWH I call, and he answered me from [the] mountain of his holiness. Selah.

en.L: [With] my voice I call to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answers me from [the] mountain of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness. Selah
en.B: I lift my voice and call to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy mountain {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answers me. Selah
en.R: I shout to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answers me from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy mountain. Selah

fr.L: [De] ma voix j’appelle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me répond de [la] montagne de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainteté. Sélah
fr.B: J’élève la voix, j’appelle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q et de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} montagne sainte {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me répond. Sélah
fr.R: J’appelle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au secours, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me répond de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} montagne sainte. Sélah

sw.L: [Kwa] sauti yangu ninamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ananijibu kutoka mlima wa utakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Sela
sw.B: Ninapaza sauti yangu na kumwita {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ananijibu kutoka mlima {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mtakatifu. Sela
sw.R: Ninamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anisaidie, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ananijibu kutoka mlima {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mtakatifu. Sela

es.L: [Con] mi voz clamo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me responde desde [el] monte de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santidad. Selah
es.B: Alzo mi voz y clamo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, \q y desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} monte santo {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me responde. Selah
es.R: Le grito {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} pidiendo ayuda, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me responde desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} monte santo. Selah

vi.L: [Bằng] tiếng tôi, tôi kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp lời tôi từ núi của sự thánh khiết của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sê-la
vi.B: Tôi cất tiếng kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q và từ núi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp lời tôi. Sê-la
vi.R: Tôi kêu lớn tiếng xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp đỡ, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trả lời tôi từ núi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sê-la

ko.L: 내 목소리로 내가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖으면, \q 그분께서 그분의 거룩함의 산에서 내게 응답하신다. 셀라
ko.B: 내가 소리 높여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖으면, \q 그분께서 거룩한 산에서 내게 응답하신다. 셀라
ko.R: 내가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 도와 달라고 외치면, \q 그분께서 거룩한 산에서 내게 대답하신다. 셀라

pt.L: [Com] a minha voz clamo {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, \q e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me responde do monte da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} santidade. Selá
pt.B: Ergo a voz e clamo {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, \q e do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} monte santo {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me responde. Selá
pt.R: Eu grito {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} pedindo socorro, \q e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me responde do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} monte santo. Selá

decisions.choice: I call, and he answers: what always happens
alternatives: I called, and he answered (that day)
decisions.reason: The first verb is in the form for ongoing or repeated action, and the second continues it. The psalmist may be telling what happened when he cried out, or what happens every time; the answer is sure either way.

decisions.choice: his holy mountain: Zion
decisions.reason: The LORD's holy mountain is Zion in Jerusalem (2:6), where the ark of the covenant stood. When David fled he sent the ark back to the city (2 Samuel 15:25), yet the LORD answers him from there.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: Verses 5-7 speak about the LORD in the plain written style with the honorific, and the psalmist is "나"
alternatives: 합쇼체 and 저 throughout the psalm
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from "you" to "he" here; Korean marks the turn as the published Psalm 23 does, and returns to 합쇼체 with "저" when verse 8 speaks to God again. A reviewer may prefer one level for the whole psalm.

source.text: אֲנִ֥י שָׁכַ֗בְתִּי וָֽאִ֫ישָׁ֥נָה הֱקִיצ֑וֹתִי כִּ֖י יְהוָ֣ה יִסְמְכֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: I, I lay down and I slept; I awoke, for YHWH sustains me.

en.L: As for me, I lay down and slept; \q I awoke, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sustains me.
en.B: I lay down and fell asleep, \q and I woke up again, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} holds me up.
en.R: I lay down and slept. \q Then I woke up again, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} takes care of me.

fr.L: Moi, je me suis couché et j’ai dormi ; \q je me suis réveillé, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me soutient.
fr.B: Je me suis couché et je me suis endormi, \q puis je me suis réveillé, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me tient debout.
fr.R: Je me suis couché et j’ai dormi. \q Ensuite je me suis réveillé, \q parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} prend soin de moi.

sw.L: Mimi, nililala nikapata usingizi; \q niliamka, \q kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ananitegemeza.
sw.B: Nililala na kupata usingizi, \q kisha nikaamka tena, \q kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ananishika.
sw.R: Nilijilaza nikalala. \q Kisha nikaamka tena, \q kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ananitunza.

es.L: En cuanto a mí, me acosté y dormí; \q desperté, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me sostiene.
es.B: Me acosté y me quedé dormido, \q y volví a despertar, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me sostiene.
es.R: Me acosté y dormí. \q Luego me desperté otra vez, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me cuida.

vi.L: Còn tôi, tôi đã nằm xuống và ngủ; \q tôi đã thức dậy, \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nâng đỡ tôi.
vi.B: Tôi nằm xuống và ngủ thiếp đi, \q rồi tôi lại thức dậy, \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nâng đỡ tôi.
vi.R: Tôi nằm xuống và ngủ. \q Rồi tôi lại thức dậy, \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} chăm sóc tôi.

ko.L: 나로 말하면, 나는 누워 잠들었고, \q 깨어났다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 붙드시기 때문이다.
ko.B: 나는 누워 잠이 들었다가 \q 다시 깨어났다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 붙들어 주시기 때문이다.
ko.R: 나는 누워서 잤다. \q 그리고 다시 깨어났다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 돌보아 주시기 때문이다.

pt.L: Quanto a mim, eu me deitei e dormi; \q acordei, \q porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me ampara.
pt.B: Eu me deitei e adormeci, \q e acordei de novo, \q porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me mantém de pé.
pt.R: Eu me deitei e dormi. \q Depois acordei de novo, \q porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} cuida de mim.

decisions.choice: I lay down and slept; I awoke: last night
alternatives: I lie down and sleep; I wake (always)
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the past form: he lay down, slept and woke, though enemies were all around. Some read them as what he always does. Either way, sleep in the middle of danger shows his trust.

decisions.choice: sustains: holds up, supports
decisions.reason: The verb (samak) means to lean on or hold up (Psalm 37:24: the LORD holds the righteous up by the hand). The LORD kept him through the night.

decisions.choice: As for me
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is stated for emphasis at the start; Literal shows it.

source.text: לֹֽא־אִ֭ירָא מֵרִבְב֥וֹת עָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר סָ֝בִ֗יב שָׁ֣תוּ עָלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Not I will fear from ten thousands of people who all around have set against me.

en.L: I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people \q who all around have set themselves against me.
en.B: I have no fear of the tens of thousands \q who have taken up positions against me on every side.
en.R: I will not be afraid, \q even if thousands and thousands of people surround me to attack me.

fr.L: Je n’aurai pas peur des myriades de gens \q qui, tout autour, se sont postés contre moi.
fr.B: Je ne crains pas les dizaines de milliers \q qui se sont déployés contre moi de tous côtés.
fr.R: Je n’aurai pas peur, \q même si des milliers et des milliers de gens m’entourent pour m’attaquer.

sw.L: Sitaogopa makumi elfu ya watu \q ambao pande zote wamejipanga dhidi yangu.
sw.B: Sina hofu ya makumi elfu ya watu \q waliojipanga kunishambulia kila upande.
sw.R: Sitaogopa, \q hata kama maelfu na maelfu ya watu wakinizunguka ili kunishambulia.

es.L: No tendré miedo de decenas de miles de personas \q que a mi alrededor se han apostado contra mí.
es.B: No temo a las decenas de miles \q que han tomado posiciones contra mí por todos lados.
es.R: No tendré miedo, \q aunque miles y miles de personas me rodeen para atacarme.

vi.L: Tôi sẽ không sợ hàng vạn người \q là những kẻ đã dàn trận khắp chung quanh chống lại tôi.
vi.B: Tôi chẳng sợ hàng chục ngàn quân \q đã dàn trận chống lại tôi từ mọi phía.
vi.R: Tôi sẽ không sợ hãi, \q dù có hàng ngàn hàng vạn người vây quanh để tấn công tôi.

ko.L: 나는 수만의 백성을 두려워하지 않을 것이다, \q 사방에서 나를 대적하여 진 친 자들을.
ko.B: 나는 수만 명이라도 두렵지 않다, \q 사방에서 나를 치려고 진을 친 자들이라 해도.
ko.R: 나는 두려워하지 않을 것이다. \q 수많은 사람이 나를 둘러싸고 공격하려 해도 두렵지 않다.

pt.L: Não terei medo de dezenas de milhares de pessoas \q que ao redor se puseram contra mim.
pt.B: Não tenho medo das dezenas de milhares \q que tomaram posição contra mim por todos os lados.
pt.R: Não vou ter medo, \q mesmo que milhares e milhares de pessoas me cerquem para me atacar.

decisions.choice: ten thousands: a number too large to count
decisions.reason: The word (rebabah) means ten thousand, and in the plural a vast number (Deuteronomy 33:17). Absalom gathered "all Israel" against David (2 Samuel 17:11).

decisions.choice: have set themselves: taken up positions, as an army does
decisions.reason: The verb (shit) means to set or place; used of people against someone it means to take up positions to attack (Isaiah 22:7).

source.text: ק֘וּמָ֤ה יְהוָ֨ה׀הוֹשִׁ֘יעֵ֤נִי אֱלֹהַ֗י כִּֽי־הִכִּ֣יתָ אֶת־כָּל־אֹיְבַ֣י לֶ֑חִי שִׁנֵּ֖י רְשָׁעִ֣ים שִׁבַּֽרְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Arise, YHWH! Save me, my God! For you have struck all my enemies [on the] cheek; [the] teeth of wicked [people] you have broken.

en.L: Arise, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! Save me, my God! \q For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have struck all my enemies [on the] cheek; \q [the] teeth of [the] wicked {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have broken.
en.B: Rise up, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! Rescue me, my God! \q For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have struck all my enemies across the jaw \q and smashed the teeth of the wicked.
en.R: Get up, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! Save me, my God! \q You have hit all my enemies in the face. \q You have broken the teeth of wicked people so that they cannot bite.

fr.L: Lève-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Sauve-moi, mon Dieu ! \q Car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as frappé tous mes ennemis [à la] joue ; \q [les] dents des méchants, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} [les] as brisées.
fr.B: Debout, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Délivre-moi, mon Dieu ! \q Car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as frappé tous mes ennemis à la mâchoire \q et fracassé les dents des méchants.
fr.R: Lève-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Sauve-moi, mon Dieu ! \q Tu as frappé tous mes ennemis au visage. \q Tu as cassé les dents des méchants pour qu’ils ne puissent plus mordre.

sw.L: Inuka, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Uniokoe, Ee Mungu wangu! \q Kwa maana umewapiga adui zangu wote shavuni; \q meno ya waovu umeyavunja.
sw.B: Simama, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Uniokoe, Mungu wangu! \q Kwa maana umewapiga adui zangu wote tayani \q na kuyavunja meno ya waovu.
sw.R: Amka, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Uniokoe, Mungu wangu! \q Umewapiga adui zangu wote usoni. \q Umevunja meno ya watu waovu ili wasiweze kuuma.

es.L: ¡Levántate, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! ¡Sálvame, Dios mío! \q Porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has golpeado a todos mis enemigos [en la] mejilla; \q [los] dientes de [los] malvados has quebrado.
es.B: ¡Álzate, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! ¡Rescátame, Dios mío! \q Porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} has golpeado a todos mis enemigos en la quijada \q y has roto los dientes de los malvados.
es.R: ¡Levántate, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! ¡Sálvame, Dios mío! \q Tú has golpeado a todos mis enemigos en la cara. \q Les has roto los dientes a los malvados para que no puedan morder.

vi.L: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin trỗi dậy! Đức Chúa Trời của tôi ơi, xin cứu tôi! \q Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đánh vào má mọi kẻ thù của tôi; \q răng của kẻ ác, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã bẻ gãy.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin hãy đứng dậy! Đức Chúa Trời của tôi ơi, xin giải cứu tôi! \q Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đánh vào hàm mọi kẻ thù của tôi \q và đập gãy răng của kẻ ác.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin hãy đứng lên! Đức Chúa Trời của tôi ơi, xin cứu tôi! \q Ngài đã đánh vào mặt mọi kẻ thù của tôi. \q Ngài đã bẻ gãy răng của kẻ ác để chúng không còn cắn được nữa.

ko.L: 일어나십시오, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여! 저를 구원하십시오, 저의 하나님! \q 참으로 주님께서 제 모든 원수의 뺨을 치셨고, \q 악인들의 이를 부러뜨리셨습니다.
ko.B: 일어나십시오, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여! 저를 건져 주십시오, 저의 하나님! \q 주님께서 제 모든 원수의 턱을 치시고 \q 악인들의 이를 부수셨습니다.
ko.R: 일어나십시오, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여! 저를 구해 주십시오, 저의 하나님! \q 주님께서 제 원수들의 얼굴을 모두 치셨습니다. \q 악한 사람들이 물지 못하도록 그들의 이를 부러뜨리셨습니다.

pt.L: Levanta-te, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}! Salva-me, meu Deus! \q Porque {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} feriste todos os meus inimigos [na] face; \q os dentes dos ímpios {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} quebraste.
pt.B: Levanta-te, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}! Livra-me, meu Deus! \q Pois {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} golpeaste todos os meus inimigos no queixo \q e quebraste os dentes dos ímpios.
pt.R: Levanta-te, {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}! Salva-me, meu Deus! \q Tu bateste no rosto de todos os meus inimigos. \q Tu quebraste os dentes das pessoas más, para que elas não possam morder.

decisions.choice: Arise, LORD: the cry when the ark set out
decisions.reason: "Arise, LORD" was Moses' cry when the ark set out before Israel: "let your enemies be scattered" (Numbers 10:35). It calls on God to act as a warrior.

decisions.choice: you have struck, you have broken: what God has done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the past form. They may tell what the LORD has done before, the ground of the prayer; or they may speak of a coming victory as if it were already done. Some read them as requests.

decisions.choice: struck on the cheek, broken teeth: enemies humiliated and made harmless
decisions.reason: A blow on the cheek is an insult (1 Kings 22:24; Micah 5:1). The wicked are pictured as wild animals whose teeth are broken so they can no longer tear (Job 29:17).

decisions.choice: so that they cannot bite
decisions.reason: Readable says what breaking the teeth means (m3).

decisions.choice: Rise up (B); Get up (R)
decisions.reason: "Arise" is old-fashioned outside the Bible; Literal keeps it to show the echo of Numbers 10:35 (m1).

decisions.choice: "xin" before each request to God, and "Đức Chúa Trời của tôi ơi" for "my God"
decisions.reason: A bare command to God would be rude in Vietnamese, so each request takes "xin", the word of asking the grammar of prayer requires; it is not bracketed at Literal, as in Psalm 139:23. "ơi" is the ordinary word of calling after a name or title.

decisions.choice: "악인" (L, B) and "악한 사람" (R) for the wicked
decisions.reason: Terms note (recurring terms), as the published Psalm 1; the same words stand for the wicked through Psalms 3-25.

decisions.choice: Levanta-te (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the English varies "Arise" (L), "Rise up" (B), "Get up" (R) because "arise" is old-fashioned. Portuguese "Levanta-te" is the ordinary word at every level and is the cry of Numbers 10:35 in its Portuguese (m1), so all three levels keep it.

records.literal_gloss: To YHWH [belongs] the salvation; upon your people [be] your blessing. Selah.

en.L: To {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [belongs] salvation; \q on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people [be] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blessing. Selah
en.B: It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who saves. \q Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} blessing rest on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. Selah
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the one who saves. \q Please bless {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. Selah

fr.L: {{divine_name:Au SEIGNEUR|À Yahvé}} [appartient] le salut ; \q sur {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple [soit] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bénédiction ! Sélah
fr.B: C’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui sauve. \q Que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bénédiction repose sur {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple ! Sélah
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est celui qui sauve. \q Bénis {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple ! Sélah

sw.L: Wokovu [ni] wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q juu ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} [iwe] baraka {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. Sela
sw.B: Ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anayeokoa. \q Baraka {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na ikae juu ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}. Sela
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ndiye anayeokoa. \q Tafadhali wabariki watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}. Sela

es.L: {{divine_name:Del SEÑOR|De Yahvé}} [es] la salvación; \q sobre {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo [sea] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} bendición. Selah
es.B: Es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien salva. \q Que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} bendición repose sobre {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo. Selah
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es el que salva. \q Por favor, bendice a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo. Selah

vi.L: Sự cứu rỗi [thuộc về] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; \q phước lành của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [ở] trên dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sê-la
vi.B: Chính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} là Đấng giải cứu. \q Nguyện phước lành của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở trên dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sê-la
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} là Đấng cứu giúp. \q Xin ban phước cho dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Sê-la

ko.L: 구원은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 [있습니다]. \q 주님의 백성 위에 주님의 복이 [있기를 빕니다]. 셀라
ko.B: 구원하시는 분은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}이십니다. \q 주님의 복이 주님의 백성 위에 머물게 해 주십시오. 셀라
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 구원하시는 분이십니다. \q 주님의 백성에게 복을 내려 주십시오. 셀라

pt.L: {{divine_name:Ao SENHOR|A Javé}} [pertence] a salvação; \q sobre o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo [esteja] a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} bênção. Selá
pt.B: É {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} quem salva. \q Que a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} bênção repouse sobre o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo. Selá
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é aquele que salva. \q Por favor, abençoa o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} povo. Selá

decisions.choice: To the LORD belongs salvation: rescue is his to give
decisions.reason: The word for salvation (yeshu'ah) answers the enemies of verse 3, who said there was no salvation for him in God. Rescue is the LORD's, and only he gives it (Jonah 2:9).

decisions.choice: on your people your blessing: a prayer
alternatives: your blessing is on your people (a statement)
decisions.reason: The line has no verb. It is most naturally a prayer, ending a psalm that began in danger with a blessing for all the people, though some of them had turned against the king.

decisions.choice: who saves (B); the one who saves (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the noun into a verb (compare verse 3); Literal keeps "salvation".

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: "sự cứu rỗi" (L); "Đấng giải cứu" (B); "Đấng cứu giúp" (R)
decisions.reason: The word here is rescue from danger, not only the salvation of the soul that "sự cứu rỗi" calls to mind in church language. Literal keeps the key term; Balanced and Readable say it as the English does, "the one who saves".
